## Notes

The estimated time for this lab is around 1h15.

**We will not run `cellranger` in this lab**: it is not available in the
workshop environment (see below). The two `cellranger` commands of this lab
(`cellranger mkfastq` and `cellranger count`) were run beforehand by the
instructors, with `cellranger` 7.1.0, on the same data. Their output is shown
below, and **all the files they produced are available in your session**, in
the (read-only) `~/Share/data_wrangling/` folder. All the other commands of
this lab read these files: run them in your terminal!

:::

::: {.callout-tip icon='true'}

## Aims

- Learn how to demultiplex sequencing data using `cellranger mkfastq`.
- Learn how to generate gene count matrices using `cellranger count`.
- Explore the outputs of both commands.

:::

::: {.callout-warning icon='true'}

## Running `cellranger` on your own data

[`cellranger`](https://www.10xgenomics.com/support/software/cell-ranger/latest)
is distributed by 10x Genomics under its own end-user license agreement, and
requires a pre-built transcriptome reference (~10 GB for the mouse reference
used here): neither is included in the workshop environment. To run it on
your own machine, download `cellranger` from the
[10x Genomics website](https://www.10xgenomics.com/support/software/cell-ranger/downloads)
and a pre-built reference from [here](https://www.10xgenomics.com/support/software/cell-ranger/downloads#reference-downloads).

`cellranger mkfastq` additionally relies on Illumina's `bcl2fastq`, and recent
`cellranger` releases deprecate it in favour of Illumina's `BCL Convert`. Check
the documentation of the version you use: e.g., since `cellranger` 8.0,
`cellranger count` also requires a `--create-bam true` (or `false`) argument.

:::

## Demultiplexing sequencing data with `cellranger mkfastq`

Navigate to your terminal in `RStudio`.

Go to the [cellranger mkfastq page](https://www.10xgenomics.com/support/software/cell-ranger/latest/analysis/inputs/cr-mkfastq)
and read the **Overview**.

For this workshop, we are going to look at a toy dataset provided by 10x
Genomics: `cellranger-tiny-bcl-1.2.0`, a sequencing run folder containing
`.bcl` files. It comes with a samplesheet file,
`cellranger-tiny-bcl-simple-1.2.0.csv`, which contains the sample
information. Both are available in the `~/Share/data_wrangling/` folder, along
with the outputs of `cellranger mkfastq` (`tiny-bcl/`) and of
`cellranger count` (`counts/`):

```{sh filename="bash"}
ls -l ~/Share/data_wrangling/
```

::: {.callout-note icon='true'}
## Where do these files come from?

The run folder was downloaded from 10x Genomics (no need to run this):

```{sh eval=FALSE, filename="bash"}
wget https://cf.10xgenomics.com/supp/cell-exp/cellranger-tiny-bcl-1.2.0.tar.gz
tar -xzf cellranger-tiny-bcl-1.2.0.tar.gz
```

Note that the samplesheet currently distributed by 10x Genomics
(<https://cf.10xgenomics.com/supp/cell-exp/cellranger-tiny-bcl-simple-1.2.0.csv>)
lists a different sample index set (`SI-P03-C9`) from the one used to produce
the outputs of this lab (`SI-GA-E3`, in `~/Share/data_wrangling/`).
:::

::: {.callout-question}
::: {.callout-note title="Question"}

Go to the Terminal tab in your `RStudio` and take a look at the 10x samplesheet `.csv` file

::: {.callout-answer}
::: {.callout-note title="Answer" collapse="true"}

```{sh filename="bash"}
cat ~/Share/data_wrangling/cellranger-tiny-bcl-simple-1.2.0.csv
```

The reads of lane `1` tagged with one of the 4 index sequences of the 10x
sample index set `SI-GA-E3` (`AGGTATTG`, `CTCCTAGT`, `TCAAGGCC`, `GATGCCAA`)
belong to the sample `test_sample`.

:::
:::

::: {.callout-question}
::: {.callout-note title="Question"}

Next, explore the contents of the sequencing directory:

::: {.callout-answer}
::: {.callout-note title="Answer" collapse="true"}

```{sh filename="bash"}
ls -l ~/Share/data_wrangling/cellranger-tiny-bcl-1.2.0
cat ~/Share/data_wrangling/cellranger-tiny-bcl-1.2.0/RunInfo.xml
```

:::
:::

:::
:::

The `.bcl` files are demultiplexed into `fastq` files with the
`cellranger mkfastq` command. Its arguments are listed in the
[cellranger mkfastq documentation](https://www.10xgenomics.com/support/software/cell-ranger/latest/analysis/inputs/cr-mkfastq)
(or with `cellranger mkfastq --help`, if `cellranger` is installed).

::: {.callout-question}
::: {.callout-note title="Question"}

What is the purpose of `--id`, `--run`, and `--csv` arguments ?

Choose these arguments wisely to demultiplex the sequencing data.

::: {.callout-answer}
::: {.callout-note title="Answer" collapse="true"}

- `--id`: the name of the pipeline run, and of the folder created to store its outputs;
- `--run`: the path to the Illumina run folder, containing the `.bcl` files;
- `--csv`: the path to the samplesheet, assigning sample index(es) to each sample, in each lane.

This is the command that was run by the instructors, from the folder
containing the run folder and the samplesheet:

```{sh eval=FALSE, filename="bash"}
## Not run: `cellranger` is not available in your session, and its outputs
## are already in ~/Share/data_wrangling/tiny-bcl/
cellranger mkfastq \
    --id tiny-bcl \
    --run cellranger-tiny-bcl-1.2.0 \
    --csv cellranger-tiny-bcl-simple-1.2.0.csv
```

The output folders can be viewed by running the `ls` command:

```{sh filename="bash"}
ls -l ~/Share/data_wrangling/tiny-bcl/outs/fastq_path
ls -l ~/Share/data_wrangling/tiny-bcl/outs/fastq_path/H35KCBCXY/test_sample
```

`cellranger mkfastq` also writes the reads which could not be assigned to any
sample in `Undetermined_*.fastq.gz` files: these were removed from
`~/Share/data_wrangling/tiny-bcl/` to save space.

::: {.callout-question}
::: {.callout-note title="Question"}

Look at the first reads listed in index read (`I1`), read 1 (`R1`), and read 2 (`R2`) files.

What is the purpose of the index read? What does it contain? And read 1?

::: {.callout-answer}
::: {.callout-note title="Answer" collapse="true"}

```{sh filename="bash"}
cd ~/Share/data_wrangling/tiny-bcl/outs/fastq_path/H35KCBCXY/test_sample
zcat test_sample_S1_L001_I1_001.fastq.gz | head -n 12
zcat test_sample_S1_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz | head -n 4
zcat test_sample_S1_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz | head -n 4
```

The index read (`I1`) contains the sample index (here, `AGGTATTG`, one of
the 4 sequences of the `SI-GA-E3` index set): it identifies the library, i.e.
the sample, each read comes from. Read 1 (`R1`, 26 bp here) contains the cell
barcode (first 16 bp) and the UMI (next 10 bp). Read 2 (`R2`) contains the
sequence of the transcript (cDNA).

:::
:::

:::
:::

Open the html file `~/Share/data_wrangling/tiny-bcl/outs/fastq_path/Reports/html/index.html`
by navigating to the file in RStudio, using the Files Tab. When you click on
the file, select the option to View in Web Browser. Take some time to explore
the demultiplexed outputs.

## Generating gene count matrices with `cellranger count`

Go to the [cellranger count algorithm overview](https://www.10xgenomics.com/support/software/cell-ranger/latest/algorithms-overview/cr-gex-algorithm)
and read the section on **Alignment** (Read Trimming, Genome Alignment, MAPQ
adjustment, Transcriptome Alignment, UMI Counting).

The `cellranger count` command generates gene count matrices from the
demultiplexed reads. Its arguments are described in the
[cellranger documentation](https://www.10xgenomics.com/support/software/cell-ranger/latest)
(or with `cellranger count --help`, if `cellranger` is installed).

The gene count matrix of the `test_sample` reads was generated with
`cellranger count` and the `refdata-gex-mm10-2020-A` mouse transcriptome
reference provided by 10x Genomics.

::: {.callout-question}
::: {.callout-note title="Question"}

What is the purpose of the `--id`, `--transcriptome`, `--fastqs` and `--sample` arguments?

::: {.callout-answer}
::: {.callout-note title="Answer" collapse="true"}

- `--id`: the name of the pipeline run, and of the folder created to store its outputs;
- `--transcriptome`: the path to the `cellranger`-compatible transcriptome reference (genome index and gene annotations);
- `--fastqs`: the path to the folder containing the `fastq` files;
- `--sample`: the prefix of the names of the `fastq` files to use (`test_sample` for `test_sample_S1_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz`, ...).

This is the command that was run by the instructors (from the same folder as
`cellranger mkfastq`):

```{sh eval=FALSE, filename="bash"}
## Not run: `cellranger` is not available in your session, and its outputs
## are already in ~/Share/data_wrangling/counts/
cellranger count \
    --id counts \
    --transcriptome refdata-gex-mm10-2020-A \
    --fastqs tiny-bcl/outs/fastq_path/H35KCBCXY/test_sample \
    --sample test_sample
```

And here is its output (abridged, and with the paths edited to the location
of the files in your session):

With this version of `cellranger`, reads mapped to introns are also counted
by default (`--include-introns true`), and a `BAM` file is created by default.

:::
:::

:::
:::

Read about the [format of the feature-barcode matrices](https://www.10xgenomics.com/support/software/cell-ranger/latest/analysis/outputs/cr-outputs-mex-matrices).

The pipeline outputs can be viewed with `ls`:

```{sh filename="bash"}
ls -l ~/Share/data_wrangling/counts/outs
```

::: {.callout-question}
::: {.callout-note title="Question"}

Can you locate the feature-barcode matrices? What is the difference between the
`raw_feature_bc_matrix` and `filtered_feature_bc_matrix` data types?

::: {.callout-tip icon='true'}
```{sh filename="bash"}
cd ~/Share/data_wrangling/counts/outs
ls -l raw_feature_bc_matrix.h5 filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5
ls -l raw_feature_bc_matrix/ filtered_feature_bc_matrix/
```
:::

How many cells and genes are stored in each matrix? Comment.

::: {.callout-answer}
::: {.callout-note title="Answer" collapse="true"}
```{sh filename="bash"}
# Number of genes
zcat ~/Share/data_wrangling/counts/outs/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/features.tsv.gz | wc -l
zcat ~/Share/data_wrangling/counts/outs/raw_feature_bc_matrix/features.tsv.gz | wc -l

# Number of cells
zcat ~/Share/data_wrangling/counts/outs/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/barcodes.tsv.gz | wc -l
zcat ~/Share/data_wrangling/counts/outs/raw_feature_bc_matrix/barcodes.tsv.gz | wc -l
```

Both matrices list the same genes. The raw matrix contains every barcode with
at least one UMI (i.e. mostly empty droplets), while the filtered matrix only
contains the barcodes `cellranger` called as cells.
:::
:::

Now open the html file `~/Share/data_wrangling/counts/outs/web_summary.html`
by navigating to the file in RStudio, using the Files Tab. When you click on
the file, select the option to View in Web Browser. Take some time to explore
the gene expression matrix outputs.

:::
:::

::: {.callout-question}
::: {.callout-note title="Bonus question"}

`cellranger count` also produced a `BAM` file, containing the alignment of
every read. Use `samtools` (see [Lab 1](Lab1_Intro.qmd)) to look at one of
the reads assigned to a gene. Where are the cell barcode, the UMI and the gene
of the read stored?

::: {.callout-answer}
::: {.callout-note title="Answer" collapse="true"}

```{sh filename="bash"}
samtools view -d GN ~/Share/data_wrangling/counts/outs/possorted_genome_bam.bam | head -n 1 | tr '\t' '\n'
```

After the 11 mandatory fields of each alignment, `cellranger` adds tags to
each read: `CR`/`CB` are the raw/corrected cell barcode, `UR`/`UB` the
raw/corrected UMI, and `GX`/`GN` the ID/name of the gene the read is assigned
to. Their description is available in the
[cellranger documentation](https://www.10xgenomics.com/support/software/cell-ranger/latest/analysis/outputs/cr-outputs-bam).

:::
